high.title: VN-Index Achieves Strongest Single-Day Gain in History After Vietnam Upgrade Confirmation
high.summary: The Vietnamese stock market experienced an explosive session on April 8th with the strongest single-day gain in history measured by absolute points. VN-Index surged 79.01 points (+4.71%) to 1,756.55 points, reaching its highest level in about a month. Trading volume on HOSE jumped to nearly 30,400 billion VND, approximately 40% higher than the average of the last 20 sessions. This breakthrough came after Vietnam received confirmation of its market upgrade prospects, marking a critical catalyst for foreign investment flows. However, foreign investors continued net selling 669 billion VND across the market, while securities companies' proprietary trading recorded net sales of 36 billion VND on HOSE. The surge demonstrates renewed investor confidence following geopolitical tensions in the Middle East that had previously dampened market sentiment. For fund managers, this represents a potential inflection point for Vietnamese equities, though sustained foreign inflows will be crucial for maintaining momentum.

high.title: Banks Unanimously Commit to Interest Rate Cuts
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) held a meeting where banks unanimously committed to reducing interest rates to support economic growth. New Governor Phạm Đức Ấn chaired the meeting, emphasizing coordinated monetary policy implementation. The SBV reported conducting flexible open market operations, purchasing securities daily with appropriate volumes and diverse maturities to support liquidity and stabilize the money market. Credit growth targets have been set at 15% with a focus on priority sectors including manufacturing, exports, supporting businesses, agriculture, and social housing. The central bank also managed exchange rates and foreign exchange markets appropriately to absorb shocks and maintain macroeconomic stability. This coordinated approach between the SBV and commercial banks signals potential easing in monetary conditions, which could support VND stability and government bond yields. For investors, this represents a shift toward more accommodative policy that could benefit both equities and fixed income markets.

high.title: New SBV Governor Profile: Former Agribank Chairman Takes Helm
high.summary: Phạm Đức Ấn, born in 1970 in Nghệ An province, has been appointed as the new Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam. He holds advanced degrees in political theory, economic law, banking-finance, and business administration. His extensive banking career includes positions as BIDV Branch Director in Hưng Yên, BIDV Deputy General Director, VRB General Director, and SBV Office Director. Most recently, he served as Party Secretary and Chairman of Agribank from May 2020, before briefly serving as Chairman of Quảng Ninh province and later Đà Nẵng. His appointment signals continuity in Vietnam's monetary policy framework while bringing deep commercial banking experience to the central bank. His background in agricultural finance and large state-owned bank management suggests familiarity with both policy implementation and market dynamics. For VND and bond markets, his pragmatic approach developed through commercial banking could influence how monetary policy tools are deployed, particularly regarding interest rate management and credit flow optimization.

medium.title: Fed Rate Hike Expectations Hit Record Low After US-Iran Ceasefire Agreement
medium.summary: Energy prices cooled significantly after the US-Iran ceasefire announcement, with Brent crude falling 13.5% to $94.50/barrel and WTI down 14% to $96.45/barrel. According to CME's FedWatch tool, expectations for Fed rate hikes dropped to a record low 0.8% from 11.7% earlier in the week. This global monetary easing environment could provide more room for SBV policy flexibility and support for VND stability.

medium.title: Banks Continue Raising Deposit Rates, Offering Up to 8.2% Interest on 500,000 VND Deposits
medium.summary: Vietnamese banks are continuing to raise deposit rates aggressively to compete for funding, with some offering up to 8.2% annually for online deposits. Vietcombank has launched certificate of deposits through digital banking with rates up to 7.9% annually. This intense competition for deposits reflects tight liquidity conditions and banks' need to strengthen their funding base amid strong credit growth.

medium.title: Vietcombank Interest Rates April 2026: 24-Month Term Offers Highest Rate
medium.summary: Vietcombank maintains its deposit rate ceiling at 6.5% annually in early April 2026. The bank significantly increased rates for terms of 12 months and above, with 12-month rates rising 0.7 percentage points to 5.9% annually. The 24-month term offers the highest rate at 6.5% annually, reflecting the bank's strategy to attract longer-term deposits amid funding competition.

medium.title: VN-Index Could Surpass 2,000 Points, VDSC Identifies Key Stock Groups
medium.summary: Vietcombank Securities (VDSC) estimates VN-Index trading range at 1,584-2,042 points based on adjusted P/E target of 12.5x-16.0x. The index could reach the upper band if geopolitical tensions ease and domestic policies prove effective, though the market isn't ready for quick recovery without favorable external conditions.

medium.title: ACB AGMS: Targets Over 22,300 Billion VND Profit in 2026, Plans Cash and Stock Dividends in Q2
medium.summary: ACB set ambitious profit targets exceeding 22,300 billion VND for 2026 and plans dividend payments in both cash and shares in Q2. Q1 2026 profit reached 5,400 billion VND, up 56% quarter-on-quarter and 17% year-on-year, completing 24% of annual target. Credit grew 3.2% and deposits increased 1% in Q1.

medium.title: Oil Prices Rebound After Steepest Drop in 6 Years, Iran Accuses US of Violating Agreement
medium.summary: Oil prices rebounded with Brent up 3.1% to $97.76/barrel and WTI up 3.2% to $97.44/barrel after Iran accused the US of violating ceasefire terms. This volatility in energy markets could impact Vietnam's inflation outlook and influence SBV monetary policy decisions.
